outcome_detail: Application for authorization filed December 14, 2021; authorization hearing held March 26, 2025; authorization granted May 27, 2025; originating application filed October 17, 2025. Case is proceeding toward trial in Quebec Superior Court; no settlement or judgment on the merits as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: In November 2016, Quebec's Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions announced that no charges would be laid against Sûreté du Québec officers in the 37 Val-d'Or-area files investigated by Montreal police following the 2015 allegations. Two retired provincial police officers were charged in 2016 in separate cases arising from other communities (Schefferville-related files), not the Val-d'Or allegations underlying this class action.
incident_date_approx: Allegations span decades with no temporal limit on the class; the underlying allegations became public in 2015 via Radio-Canada's Enquete reporting on Val-d'Or
description: The Val-d'Or Native Friendship Centre filed an application in Quebec Superior Court on December 14, 2021 to authorize a class action against the Attorney General of Quebec over the conduct of Sûreté du Québec officers in the MRC de la Vallée-de-l'Or. According to the application, Indigenous people in the region were subjected to discriminatory practices and abuses by SQ officers, including sexual assault, solicitation of sexual acts, physical assault, abduction, excessive force during arrest, and harassment, in violation of the Canadian and Quebec charters. The claims follow allegations first made public in 2015 by Indigenous women in Val-d'Or; a Montreal police investigation of 37 files ended in 2016 with prosecutors laying no charges against the officers involved. The class action was authorized on May 27, 2025, the originating application was filed on October 17, 2025, and the case is proceeding toward trial on behalf of all Indigenous people alleging such treatment by SQ officers in the region, with no temporal limitation.
notes: Seed year hint of 2022 appears to reflect early coverage; the authorization application was filed December 14, 2021 per class counsel. Seed hint of an authorization hearing in March 2025 confirmed (heard March 26, 2025; granted May 27, 2025).
inclusion_concern: Sexual assault and solicitation of sexual acts are expressly among the six categories of alleged misconduct, but the class action also covers non-sexual abuses (physical assault, abduction, excessive force, harassment); sexual misconduct is central to the underlying Val-d'Or scandal though not the sole basis of the claim.
